That "i.e." silently identifies (a) an apparatus-relative MEASURED coarse-grained functional with (b) the STRUCTURAL degree of the measure. The biconditional fails in both directions, and the direction that matters is experimentally dead.

(<=) FAILS, DECISIVELY. Standard quantum mechanics via the path integral is the in-corpus member of F1 that the extraction itself names (quantum_mechanics/alternative_formulations/1, Feynman 1948). Standard QM is exactly degree-2 over the full path-integral alternative set, and reproduces every cited phenomenon. Yet its MEASURED slit-labelled kappa is not bounded by 10^-2: Magana-Loaiza et al., Nature Communications 7, 13987 (2016) raised the looped-trajectory contribution "by almost two orders of magnitude" over baseline via surface-plasmon near-field enhancement, and state in terms that "a non-zero value of kappa can exist without such violation ... a consequence of the presence of exotic looped trajectories of light ... that arise in the Feynman path integral formulation," while explicitly confirming Born's rule. Independently, Namdar et al., Phys. Rev. A 107, 032211 (2023) produce genuine higher-order interference from nonlinear evolution with "a simple quantum mechanical description," and name it a loophole for experiments that try to verify Born's rule by ruling out higher-order interference. So a degree-2 F1 theory reproducing all corpus phenomena violates the stated bound by orders of magnitude. The requirement as written is false of the paradigm case it was extracted from.

(=>) ALSO FAILS. A measured |I_3| < 10^-2 over one coarse-graining does not establish degree 2; the extraction half-concedes this by wording the requirement as a bound, then reinstates the structural reading with "i.e." That is the illicit step, not a hedge.

THE REPAIR IS A TRAP, NOT A RESCUE. The only way to restore the arrow is to add auxiliary premises the extraction never declares: that the slit-labelled alternatives EXHAUST the theory's alternative set (no looped or multi-slit paths) and that evolution is linear. Neither is a corpus phenomenon; both are apparatus-modelling choices, and both are experimentally defeasible (above). Grant them, and the requirement collapses into analyticity: I_2 and I_3 are defined as fixed linear combinations of the very frequencies that constitute the phenomena (I_2 = P_AB - P_A - P_B; I_3 = P_ABC - P_AB - P_BC - P_AC + P_A + P_B + P_C), so ANY theory reproducing the measured numbers reproduces I_2 and I_3 by arithmetic, and F1 membership does no work whatever. The extraction supplies the proof of its own circularity in its stamp justification: "The stamp is O because the structural discriminators (I_2, I_3) are themselves the measured quantities." Where the claimed structure IS the measurement, the arrow phenomenon -> structure is empty. That is the archive's recorded vocabulary trap verbatim (protocol rule 5), and the cluster_note's boast that "the class restrictions [do] real, named work" is false for R1.1.

So R1.1 faces a closed dilemma with no survivor: read structurally (degree-2), it is REFUTED by Magana-Loaiza 2016 and Namdar 2023; read as the literal bound, it is analytic in its own vocabulary and forces nothing. Either branch destroys it as a structural requirement. KILLING COUNTEREXAMPLE (the Delta-model). Fix the cited data: preparations P_1 (slit 1), P_2 (slit 2), P_12 (both); screen measurement M with bins X; observed distributions p_1, p_2, p_12 with p_12 != lambda*p_1 + (1-lambda)*p_2 for all lambda in [0,1] (the Tonomura/Arndt content). Build the OPT T_Delta: state space Omega = conv{w_1, w_2, w_12}, three affinely independent vertices — the 2-simplex, i.e. literally classical probability theory on a 3-element sample space, the paradigm simplicial GPT (Barrett, PRA 75, 032304 (2007): "classical theory is a GPT where states correspond to probability distributions ... all state spaces are simplexes"). Effects: for each bin x, e_x defined on the vertices by e_x(w_1)=p_1(x), e_x(w_2)=p_2(x), e_x(w_12)=p_12(x), extended affinely, with sum_x e_x = unit effect. Assign P_1→w_1, P_2→w_2, P_12→w_12. Then T_Delta (a) is a finite-dimensional OPT, hence in F2; (b) satisfies R1.2's explicit and load-bearing representation assumption — the both-slits preparation is a state of the same state space, not a contextual re-specification of the experiment; (c) reproduces the cited statistics exactly; (d) has w_12 outside conv{w_1, w_2}, so conjunct (i) holds; and (e) has a SIMPLEX state space with no superposition anywhere, so conjunct (ii) is false. The arrow is therefore invalid as written.

WHERE THE ARROW BREAKS. Failing to lie in the convex hull of TWO DESIGNATED states is not non-simpliciality. A simplex requires only that every state have a UNIQUE decomposition into ITS OWN extreme points; Barrett 2007 identifies the non-unique decomposition of a mixed state into pure states as the generic non-classical feature. R1.2 tacitly assumes that w_1 and w_2 exhaust the relevant extreme points — an assumption nothing in the cited phenomena supplies, and one that is explicitly false in every hidden-variable reading, where the extreme points are the ontic states and the slit preparations are ordinary interior distributions.

SECOND HORN (the "marginal cases" clause). Read strictly — single-path statistics are marginals of the both-paths state under coarse-graining over a path variable — affinity of effects yields p_12 = w1*p_1 + w2*p_2 exactly, contradicting the observation: the premise class is EMPTY and the requirement is vacuously true. Read loosely — the single-path preparations are also states of the same system — the Delta-model satisfies it and kills the conclusion. Neither reading leaves a non-vacuous, unrefuted requirement.

R2.3 fails by its own pre-registered outright-refutation condition, and the failure traces to a premise it never declared.

THE KILL. R2.3's what_would_refute names two exits and grades them differently: a setting-independence-denying formulation "relativizes the split away -> FORMULATION-RELATIVE"; but "an exhibited F3 model whose single cone-confined structure reproduces the CHSH record ... would refute outright." Such models exist, are peer-reviewed, and sit INSIDE F3 as F3 is written. F3's membership conditions are only (i) reproduce the R2.1 Bell record, (ii) reproduce the R2.2 propagation record, (iii) have an underlying state satisfying setting-independence. Raymond-Robichaud (Proc. R. Soc. A, 2021; arXiv:1710.01380) proves that "every no-signalling theory with invertible dynamics has a local-realistic model. This applies in particular to unitary quantum theory." The constructed model gives each system a complete LOCAL description ("noumenal state") that is set before and independently of any setting choice — so (iii) holds — with a no-action-at-a-distance theorem making operations on A leave B's description untouched, and it is unitary quantum theory, so (i) and (ii) hold exactly as they do for standard QFT. Deutsch & Hayden (Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 456, 1759 (2000)) state the same conclusion flatly: "All information in quantum systems is, notwithstanding Bell's theorem, localised." In these formulations the structure that carries the Bell correlations IS the cone-confined local-descriptor flow — the same structure that bounds signals. That is the exact negation of R2.3's core sentence ("the structure carrying the Bell correlations cannot be the structure that bounds signals"), exhibited by a model in F3.

WHY THE ARROW BROKE: AN UNDECLARED PREMISE. R2.3 stars its forcing FORCED* on exactly one hypothesis — setting-independence — and its formalization_relative_to lists only two conditions: (i) setting-independence, (ii) reading signal structure as R2.2's cones. Bell's theorem needs a third: that each wing has a single, absolute outcome per run, since the factorization P(ab|xy,lambda)=P(a|x,lambda)P(b|y,lambda) presupposes there is one a and one b to which the probabilities attach. The community's own theorem names this premise as independent and co-equal: Bong et al., Nat. Phys. 16, 1199 (2020) prove that one of "'No-Superdeterminism', 'Locality' or 'Absoluteness of Observed Events' -- that every observed event exists absolutely, not relatively -- must be false." R2.3 stars the first, concludes about the second, and is silent on the third. The evaders above take the third exit, not the first — which is why they land in the "refutes outright" bucket rather than the "relativizes" bucket that R2.3 anticipated.

refutations.argument:
R4-3 dies on its own central parenthetical. The requirement asserts that "recovering deterministic-and-reversible (equivalently phase-space-area/information-conserving) effective dynamics is recovering Hamiltonian mechanics in full." That equivalence is false, and the cited source asserts the opposite logical order.

KILL 1 — determinism+reversibility is strictly weaker than area/information conservation, at one degree of freedom. Counterexample A (verified symbolically): the one-DoF flow (x,p) -> (e^t x, e^t p). It is deterministic and reversible in the sense the corpus entry itself spells out — it is a diffeomorphism of R^2 for every t, its inverse being the flow at -t, hence "exactly a one-to-one map between past and future states." Its Jacobian determinant is e^(2t), so it neither preserves phase-space area nor conserves information entropy, and its generating field has divergence 2 != 0, so it is not Hamiltonian. Determinism plus reversibility therefore does NOT entail area/entropy conservation, and symplectic structure IS content additional to determinism-plus-reversibility — precisely what R4-3 denies. Since the requirement's whole function is the bounding clause "no R4 requirement may demand symplectic/Hamiltonian structure as an ingredient additional to determinism-plus-reversibility," that clause is refuted at the requirement's own declared scope.

The only escape is to stipulate "reversible" as a term of art already meaning entropy-conserving (thermodynamic reversibility). That horn also kills the requirement, for a different reason: the bound then reads "symplectic structure is not additional to determinism-plus-entropy-conservation," in which entropy conservation is exactly the substantive extra ingredient the bound was denying. Either horn destroys it: on the plain reading it is false, on the stipulated reading it is circular (KILL 3) and no longer bounds anything.

KILL 2 — the arrow is inverted relative to the primary source, and the corpus entry overreaches its own quoted passage. The technical result behind the charter's CONTROL-5 six-characterization list is Carcassi & Aidala, "Hamiltonian mechanics is conservation of information entropy" (Stud. Hist. Phil. Mod. Phys. 71, 60 (2020), arXiv:2004.11569). Its abstract, verified verbatim at source, runs the derivation the other way: coordinate-independence of information entropy is what FORCES the symplectic manifold ("distributions with coordinate independent values for information entropy require that the manifold ... is charted by conjugate pairs (i.e. it is a symplectic manifold)"), and Hamilton's equations then require the FURTHER assumption of entropy conservation. Symplectic structure is a premise of the entropy statement, not a redundant consequence of determinism+reversibility. Carcassi's own earlier standalone paper — titled, pointedly, "Derivation of Hamiltonian mechanics from determinism and reversibility" (arXiv:1304.1886) — states in its body that determinism and reversibility are not alone sufficient, listing infinitesimal reducibility, continuity, energy conservation, phase-space area conservation and information-entropy conservation as further assumptions. The source author himself holds the position that refutes R4-3. R4-3 inherits that defect and hardens it into a bound on the whole cluster. This is a BASIS defect in the protocol's sense: the load-bearing citation does not say what the extraction says it says.

KILL 3 — circularity. Information entropy is not measure-free: under a diffeomorphism, S[phi*rho] = S[rho] + integral(rho log|det D phi|), so "entropy conservation" selects exactly the measure-preserving flows FOR WHICHEVER reference measure was fixed. At one DoF the canonical reference measure is the symplectic area form itself. The quantity offered as a substitute for symplectic structure is thus defined using symplectic structure. A formalization class that has already fixed the phase-space measure cannot be shown by this route not to need the symplectic form — the arrow is empty.

Area preservation at one DoF delivers a symplectic, i.e. LOCALLY Hamiltonian, flow; a single-valued global Hamiltonian exists only if iota_X omega is exact, not merely closed.
